title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: geometric-case functional equation for L-functions, where local factors need the inertia invariants of Galois representations. Notation as I read it: D is a decomposition-type (profinite) group, I is an inertia subgroup, and U runs over open normal subgroups contained in I. Mod(D|U,k) is the category of finite-dimensional k-linear D-modules on which U acts trivially, that is, D/U-modules. R(D|U,k) is its Grothendieck group.

The page says the modules E that matter (the 'virtual' ones, with finite ramification) are essentially those on which some open U acts trivially, so the relevant group is the union over U of the R(D|U,k).

For such E, I acts through the finite group I/U. Suppose |I/U| is invertible in k. Then E^I is the image of the averaging projector (1/|I/U|) Σ g ('opération moyenne'). So E ↦ E^I is an exact functor Mod(D|U,k) → Mod(D|I,k), and it induces an additive map φ_U: R(D|U,k) → R(D|I,k).

For V ⊂ U, a module killed by U is also killed by V. So there is a natural map R(D|U,k) → R(D|V,k) (inflation/inclusion, labelled 'restr.?'). The triangle with φ_U and φ_V commutes, because the invariants functor does not depend on which U is used. Passing to the limit gives a well-defined map E ↦ [E^I] on virtual representations with finite ramification. This feeds the local factors det(1 − F t | E^I) in the L-functions.
errors: Exactness of E ↦ E^I (struck out by Grothendieck: 'foncteur exact') needs the order of I/U to be invertible in k. In the ℓ-adic or modular setting this fails when the residue characteristic divides |I/U| (wild inertia). The page implicitly assumes tameness relative to k or characteristic 0; this is not stated in the visible text.

The vertical arrow R(D|V,k) ← R(D|U,k) labelled 'restr.' is really an inflation/inclusion map (modules trivial on U are trivial on V ⊂ U), not a restriction to a subgroup. Its direction in the diagram should be checked against the image.

ideas.what: Invariants under inertia as an exact functor via averaging when the image of inertia is finite of invertible order, inducing a homomorphism on Grothendieck groups.
ideas.modern_name: Inertia invariants E^I / local factor construction; Brauer-type averaging
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Artin, Serre; Grothendieck in SGA5 / Deligne's local constants)
ideas.where_published: Related material in SGA 5 (Grothendieck–Ogg–Shafarevich formula, L-functions); exact formulation unsure

ideas.what: Compatibility of φ_U with change of the open subgroup U, giving a limit map on virtual representations with finite (potentially) ramification.
ideas.modern_name: Colimit of representation rings / continuous representations of profinite groups

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping: exactness of inertia invariants for finite tame image and compatibility of the induced maps on Grothendieck groups. This is standard in the theory of local factors. The neighbouring 'pages' are Bourbaki Algèbre commutative chap. VII exercise drafts on the reverse of the reused sheets, not mathematically related.
